pages.text: Some ore veins were never ore. A decoy mine is a SecurityCraft mine wearing an OreSpawn costume — ruby, titanium, tiger's eye, or uranium — sitting in your tunnels looking exactly like payday.$(p)Stepping on one is harmless. The trap is greed: the decoy detonates on the final crack of mining progress, because the one thing every raider eventually does to ore is swing at it.

pages.title: Field Manual
pages.text: Shapeless, all four flavors: one real ore block plus one SecurityCraft mine. Each decoy copies its ore's hardness and tool rules, so it mines like the genuine article until the last half-heart of progress.$(p)In your inventory the item admits everything — 'Looks like ore. Isn't.' — and all four sit in SecurityCraft's Block Mines tab. Once placed, the disguise is total. Almost.

pages.title: The Tell
pages.text: The fairness tell: a white mote or two per second drifting off any face open to air, plus a soft tick every eight-odd seconds. Buried decoys stay quiet until someone digs close — exactly when the warning matters.

pages.title: Counterplay
pages.text: Spotted the shimmer? You have options. Right-click with wire cutters and the mine converts, in place, into a Suspicious Ore trophy — that's the Minesweeper advancement, and picking the trophy up earns It Was Never Ore.$(p)Choose violence instead and the blast is tuned for drama over craters: strength 2.8 against TNT's 4.0, no fire, shallow scarring. Survivable, memorable, and in creative mode it never triggers at all.

pages.title: Suspicious Ore
pages.text: Proof somebody tried to bait you and you out-played them. Breaks by hand, no tool gate, always drops itself — even with the thread toggled off — and displays beautifully next to the pickaxe that nearly did it.$(p)You mined the vein. The vein disagreed. You won anyway.
